text: I've seen so many companies do extremely well with it, and I would say that not all companies will be successful, period. Companies that are really successful with it are companies that... I think I can swear a little, they have their shit together.
speaker: Christina Wodtke
context: Lenny inquires about the impact of OKRs on companies and asks Christina to share insights on their effectiveness. Christina asserts that successful companies using OKRs have a solid foundation, including strategy and empowered teams. She emphasizes that OKRs should not be seen as a cure-all but rather as a tool that amplifies existing strengths.
text_ko: 많은 회사들이 그걸로 정말 잘 되는 걸 봤어요. 하지만 모든 회사가 성공할 수 있는 건 아니에요. 진짜 성공하는 회사들은... 솔직히 말하자면, 그들은 정말 잘 정리되어 있어요.
text_zh: 我看到很多公司在这方面表现非常出色，但我必须说，并不是所有公司都能成功。那些真正成功的公司，都是那些……我想我可以稍微直白一点，他们的管理非常到位。
text_es: He visto a muchas empresas tener un gran éxito con ello, y diría que no todas las empresas tendrán éxito, punto. Las empresas que realmente tienen éxito son aquellas que... creo que puedo decirlo de esta manera, tienen todo bajo control.
key_sentence: Successful companies have their shit together to thrive with OKRs.

vocabulary.definition: Achieving desired aims or attaining prosperity, often measured by financial performance or market position.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a successful company is one that meets its goals, whether in terms of revenue, customer satisfaction, or market share.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'successful' generally has a positive connotation, it can also imply that the means of achieving success may not always align with ethical standards.

text: I say OKRs are more of a vitamin, they're not a medicine. So, if you take OKRs and you're like, 'Oh, this will fix everything that's wrong with you.' No, that's not going to happen.
speaker: Christina Wodtke
context: Lenny wants to highlight the benefits of OKRs and how they can lead to organizational success. Christina illustrates that OKRs should be viewed as a preventative measure that enhances a company’s existing capabilities instead of a fix for underlying issues. She explains that instead of solving problems, OKRs will expose them, necessitating prior organizational health for effective implementation.
text_ko: 저는 목표와 핵심 결과(OKRs)가 약이라기보다는 비타민에 가깝다고 말해요. 그래서 OKRs를 도입해서 '이걸로 우리 조직의 모든 문제가 다 해결되겠네'라고 생각하면, 그건 아니에요.
text_zh: 我觉得OKR更像是维生素，不是药。如果你指望着用OKR来解决所有问题，觉得"这下什么毛病都能治好了"，那你就想多了，根本不是这么回事。
text_es: Yo digo que los OKRs son más como una vitamina, no un medicamento. O sea, si implementas OKRs pensando 'ay, esto va a arreglar todos mis problemas,' pues no, eso no va a pasar.
key_sentence: OKRs reveal everything wrong with your company, not a cure-all.
original_text: I say OKRs are more of a vitamin, they're not a medicine. So, if you take OKRs and you're like, 'Oh, this will fix everything that's wrong with you.' No, that's not going to happen. It's just going to reveal everything that's wrong with your company.

text: The main benefit is that there's a lot of concrete action through an OKR that you don't always get from strategy. Strategy tends to be a little longer, a little more Muji Muji.
speaker: Christina Wodtke
context: Lenny asks Christina to summarize the primary benefits of using OKRs for organizations. Christina explains that OKRs provide actionable and measurable outcomes, while strategies can often be vague and abstract. By implementing OKRs, teams can establish concrete steps towards achieving their goals, thereby creating accountability and progress.
text_ko: 주요 장점은 OKR을 통해 구체적인 행동이 많이 나온다는 거예요. 전략에서는 항상 그런 게 나오지 않거든요. 전략은 좀 더 긴 시간과 모호한 부분이 있는 것 같아요.
text_zh: 主要的好处在于，通过OKR（目标与关键结果）可以实现很多具体的行动，而这些在战略中并不总是能得到。战略往往比较长远，有些模糊。
text_es: El principal beneficio es que hay mucha acción concreta a través de un OKR (Objectives and Key Results) que no siempre se obtiene de la estrategia. La estrategia tiende a ser un poco más prolongada, un poco más abstracta.
key_sentence: there's a lot of concrete action through an OKR that you don't always get from strategy.

vocabulary.definition: A plan of action designed to achieve a long-term or overall aim, often involving the allocation of resources.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, strategy encompasses the overarching goals and methods that guide an organization toward achieving its vision and competitive advantage.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'strategy' often implies a comprehensive and long-term approach, contrasting with more immediate or tactical actions.

text: One of the biggest problems founders struggle with is they don't scale very well, but if you can set a good OKR and get people to work on it, then you don't have to decide all those little IC tasks.
speaker: Christina Wodtke
context: Lenny prompts Christina to discuss the advantages of OKRs in scaling organizations. Christina points out that an effective OKR framework allows leaders to focus on high-level objectives rather than micromanaging individual contributor tasks. This strategic approach helps in maintaining clarity and efficiency as a company grows.
text_ko: 창업자들이 가장 힘들어하는 문제 중 하나는 잘 확장되지 않는다는 거예요. 하지만 좋은 OKR(목표 및 핵심 결과)을 설정하고 사람들이 그에 맞춰 일하게 하면, 작은 IC(개별 기여자) 작업들을 일일이 결정할 필요가 없어요.
text_zh: 创始人面临的最大问题之一是他们的扩展能力有限，但如果能够设定一个良好的OKR（目标与关键成果），并让团队围绕这个目标工作，那么就不必亲自决定所有的小的个体贡献（IC）任务。
text_es: Uno de los mayores problemas que enfrentan los fundadores es que no escalan muy bien, pero si puedes establecer un buen OKR (Objective and Key Results) y lograr que las personas trabajen en él, entonces no tendrás que decidir sobre todas esas pequeñas tareas individuales.
key_sentence: if you can set a good OKR and get people to work on it, then you don't have to decide all those little IC tasks.

vocabulary.definition: To increase in size, capacity, or scope, particularly in a manner that maintains efficiency and effectiveness.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, scaling refers to the ability of a company to grow and manage increased demand without compromising performance or losing revenue potential.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'scale' often implies growth, it also suggests the need for sustainable practices and systems that can handle larger operations.

vocabulary.definition: An acronym for Objectives and Key Results, a goal-setting framework used to define measurable goals and track their outcomes.
vocabulary.businessContext: OKRs are commonly employed in organizations to align team efforts with broader company objectives, fostering transparency and accountability.
vocabulary.nuance: While OKRs are effective for setting ambitious goals, they require regular review and adjustment to remain relevant and achievable.

vocabulary.definition: Specific actions or pieces of work that need to be completed as part of a project or to achieve a goal.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, tasks are often assigned to individuals or teams to ensure that objectives are met efficiently and effectively, forming the building blocks of project management.
vocabulary.nuance: While tasks are essential for operational success, focusing too much on them can detract from the broader strategic vision if not aligned with higher-level objectives.

text: You have to think about, if somebody doesn't know what to do and you're like, 'Well, I have a strategy.
speaker: Christina Wodtke
context: Lenny asks Christina about the root causes of issues that arise with OKRs. Christina explains that if team members are unclear about their tasks or objectives, it reflects a failure in communication or strategic clarity from leadership. This highlights the importance of transparent and effective communication in fostering a productive work environment.
text_ko: 생각해봐야 해요. 누군가 뭘 해야 할지 모를 때, 당신이 “음, 난 전략(strategy)이 있어요”라고 말한다고 가정해 보세요.
text_zh: 你得这么想，如果有人不知道该怎么办，你就说："没事，我有策略。
text_es: Tienes que pensar en esto: si alguien no sabe qué hacer y tú le dices, 'Bueno, yo tengo una estrategia.'
key_sentence: if somebody doesn't know what to do
original_text: You have to think about, if somebody doesn't know what to do and you're like, 'Well, I have a strategy. I told you what my strategy is.' And they don't know how to make decisions, it means something's wrong with the strategy or you aren't being clear.

vocabulary.definition: A plan of action designed to achieve a long-term or overall aim.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a strategy outlines how an organization will allocate resources to achieve specific goals and maintain a competitive advantage.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'strategy' implies a well-thought-out plan, it can sometimes carry the connotation of being overly rigid or lacking adaptability.

text: You can either buy the obvious off-the-rack package like an NPS, or you can dig a little harder and figure out what would be meaningful to your company.
speaker: Christina Wodtke
context: Lenny discusses the challenges of measuring qualitative outcomes in product development. Christina encourages leaders to either utilize standard metrics like Net Promoter Score (NPS) or invest time in understanding what metrics would provide meaningful insights specific to their company. This underscores the importance of tailored measurement strategies to accurately assess user satisfaction and product impact.
text_ko: 당연히 NPS 같은 뻔한 패키지를 사는 것도 좋지만, 조금 더 깊이 파고들어서 우리 회사에 진짜 의미 있는 게 뭔지 알아보는 것도 중요해요.
text_zh: 您可以选择购买像NPS这样的现成解决方案，或者深入挖掘，找出对您的公司真正有意义的内容。
text_es: Puedes optar por comprar un paquete estándar como un NPS, o puedes profundizar un poco más y descubrir qué sería realmente significativo para tu empresa.
key_sentence: you can dig a little harder and figure out what would be meaningful to your company.

vocabulary.definition: Having significance or purpose; conveying an important message or value.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'meaningful' often refers to insights or metrics that provide valuable information for decision-making and strategy development.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'meaningful' suggests depth and relevance, it can be overused in contexts where data may not truly hold significance.
